desc: ERNIE (NeurIPS 2023) on URB. paper/BASELINES.md B9.
Host block == ippo/config1.json.
lam, perturb_steps  -> abukharin3/ERNIE Algorithms/configs/
config_qcombo_adv.py (config.alg.lam = 0.5, perturb_num_steps = 1).
eps -> the paper grid-searches epsilon and lambda per environment
(Appendix F); 0.1 in RELATIVE units is the value this repo runs and
is declared here rather than tuned on returns.
alpha: 0 -> alpha = eps. With one PGD step and an l2-normalised
direction that is the exact solution of the linearised inner max,
i.e. the l2 FGSM attack.
relative -> the released code's `* torch.abs(obs)` scaling, which URB
needs because its observation mixes a start time in seconds with
route counts. See CHECKLIST_ernie.md item EPS-2.
D = KL: paper Section 5.1, 'when optimizing stochastic policies (e.g.,
MAPPO), D can be taken to be the KL divergence'.
MEASURED PROPERTY OF URB'S SHIPPED NETWORKS, 2026-09-19: the median
origin-destination pair carries exactly ONE traveller on all seven of them
only 0.7-3.2% of travellers ever have an EARLIER same-OD peer -- except on
ingolstadt_custom, where it is 70%. So on saint_arnoult the observation's
four count coordinates are zero for 97% of travellers on every day of the
run. Three defaults below follow from that; see the checklist item named.
scale_floor = 1.0 (NOT the released 0.0): the released relative
scaling multiplies the perturbation by |o|, so a coordinate
that is exactly zero is never perturbed -- which on URB is
four of the five coordinates. The floor is one traveller, the
natural quantum of a count. scale_floor = 0.0 restores the
released behaviour. See CHECKLIST_ernie.md ADAPT-1.
